tasks.name: Pre-Request - Counselor Recommendation
tasks.applicability: Once for all Apps when associated requirement is selected
tasks.when: Grade 11: April, May, June | Grade12: August, September
tasks.description:
Check with your high school counselor on the proper procedure for requesting your Counselor Recommendation.  

A counselor recommendation is a form that your high school counselor completes specifically about you. Questions about you as a student and your character. 

Consult your high school counselor about the process your school follows for obtaining a Counselor Recommendation.

Inquire if your high school counselor requires any supporting materials, such as student or parent surveys, brag packets, or resumes, to assist in writing your recommendation letter.

Pro-Tips: 

Include this in your request for all College Application Requirements (such as requesting letters of recommendation from teachers, counselors, or others; transcripts; school reports; mid-year reports; and FERPA approval via systems like Scoir, Naviance, Xello, or directly in applications like the Common App). Ask if it would be acceptable to communicate with them over the summer via email when school is not in session or during busy times at the start of the year. If so, request their email address and be sure to express your gratitude!

Request this at least a few weeks in advance to give your recommender time to write your recommendation.

tasks.description:
Before submitting your test scores, you should strategize to determine which schools to send them to. 

Now that certain schools are test-blind, test-optional, or test-required, consider submitting your scores to test-optional schools only when your scores fall within the mid-range or are well above the average for students in the past for your specific major. 

To submit your scores, log into your College Board account, select the scores and the schools you want to send them to, and pay the respective fees. 

* Note—Some colleges will allow you to self-report your SAT Test scores on your application and may not require you to submit them until after you have been accepted, unless a college specifically requests them during their review of your application.
